classification.difficultyReason: Identify a day as one trial and express an exact binomial probability.

content.prompt: The probability that a small earthquake occurs somewhere in the world on any one day is 0.95. Assuming that earthquake frequencies on successive days are independent, what is the probability that a small earthquake occurs somewhere in the world on exactly 28 of January’s 31 days? Leave your answer in index form.

answer.worked:
Let $X$ be the number of January days on which a small earthquake occurs somewhere in the world. Then $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(31,0.95)$.
$$\begin{align*}P(X=28)&=\binom{31}{28}(0.95)^{28}(1-0.95)^{31-28}\\&=\binom{31}{28}(0.95)^{28}(0.05)^3\end{align*}$$
